args_observed.first: a pointer loaded from the caller's stack
args_observed.stack_arg: a caller stack address, pushed before the call and popped after; not read by this window

caller_census.method: full .text e8/e9 scan plus whole-file qword scan

exception_paths.canary: fs:0x28 saved at rsp+0x28, checked on the normal return and on the pads
exception_paths.lsda_mapping: not claimed: which landing pad serves which call site is not recorded
exception_paths.node_cleanup_pad: begin catch, operator delete of the 0x78-byte node, rethrow
exception_paths.string_dispose_pad: dispose the node's key string, delete the node, then the table cleanup pad
exception_paths.table_cleanup_pad: end catch, call 0x51524b0 (chain disposal: walks the head at table+0x10 and disposes each node's key string), then _Unwind_Resume

hash_path.below_limit_rule: element count <= 20 inserts directly with no bucket walk
hash_path.bucket_rule: unsigned hash remainder modulo the bucket count

bucket_walk.chain_end_rule: the next node is null: insert
bucket_walk.duplicate_arm_note: the arm checks the before-node's next pointer; on every consistent walk that pointer is the matched node itself, so the arm's insert branch cannot fire from a consistent table; implemented literally in the model
bucket_walk.duplicate_rule: skip the record; the next record goes straight to the hash path
bucket_walk.entry_rule: the bucket entry is the before-node; an empty entry means insert
bucket_walk.key_rules: cached hash equal, then length equal, then memcmp (skipped for empty keys)
bucket_walk.segment_end_rule: the next node's bucket differs from the target bucket: insert

init.heap_arm: allocate next count * 8 bytes via operator new, zeroed via memset

single_bucket_arm.effect: the +0x30 slot is zeroed, no allocation
single_bucket_arm.reachability: unreachable from this init: the count is set to 1 immediately above, so the skip arm takes every count of 1; recorded as observed, not as a live path

init.skip_arm: initial count >= next count: keep the single-bucket slot

insert.count_update: element count incremented by 1 after linking
insert.empty_bucket_rule: prepend to the chain head; when an old head exists its bucket entry is repointed at the new node; the new bucket's entry becomes the before-begin sentinel address (table+0x10)

key_copy.heap_rule: heap buffer via _M_create, capacity at node+0x18, memcpy of the bytes, NUL terminator after the bytes
key_copy.len_1_rule: a single byte is copied directly, no memcpy call
key_copy.sso_rule: inline buffer at node+0x18, length at node+0x10, NUL terminator after the bytes

need_rehash_call.result: need flag in al, new count in rdx
need_rehash_call.saved_slot: table+0x28 copied to a stack slot before the call

insert.nonempty_bucket_rule: insert after the before-node: new node next = before-node next, before-node next = new node

rehash_call.post_call_rule: the bucket is recomputed as hash modulo the new count, then insertion proceeds

linear_scan.empty_key_rule: walk while a node's length is nonzero; the first zero-length node means duplicate; chain end means not found
linear_scan.nonempty_key_rule: walk the chain; length equal and memcmp equal means duplicate, otherwise advance; chain end means not found

unknowns: the payload fields at node+0x28..+0x70 (copied verbatim, meanings not claimed)
the wrapper/owner identities behind the table, keys and payloads
the _M_next_bkt prime table and the _M_need_rehash internals (both PLT callees, injected as callables in the model)
the _Hash_bytes internals (PLT callee, injected as a callable)
the role of the caller's fifth stack argument (not read by this window)
which landing pad serves which call site (LSDA mapping not claimed)
the single-bucket store arm's reachability (see init.single_bucket_arm)
the duplicate arm's insert branch (see hash_path.bucket_walk.duplicate_arm_note)

args.stack_arg: pushed by the caller, not read by this window

window.returns: void; the table is the result
